title: Telemetry-driven prefix bucketing and confidence-weighted TTL annealing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a telemetry-driven system that groups cache keys into lightweight prefix buckets based on observed hit patterns, and applies a confidence-weighted TTL annealing algorithm to recommend safe TTL adjustments. The goal is to reduce unnecessary backend tokenization and model compute by improving prefix-level cache efficiency while providing a staged, observable safe-apply/rollback path for production deployments.
background: Current KV prefix TTL tuning is manual and conservative: PMs and runtime engineers pick broad TTL values which under-optimize cost for frequent short-lived prefixes and over-cache low-value prefixes. Existing autotuners operate at per-prefix scale with brittle thresholds and limited telemetry fusion. We need an approach that (1) aggregates behavior to reduce variance, (2) quantifies confidence before making changes, and (3) provides automated rollback triggers tied to latency/cost/KPI regressions.
goals: Create prefix bucketing algorithm that groups keys by recent hit-rate shape and cost-per-miss
Implement confidence-weighted TTL annealing that proposes incremental TTL changes rather than one-shot flips
Provide a staged rollout harness (dry-run -> shadow -> canary -> global) with automatic rollback gates based on telemetry
Ship UI/console surface that surfaces recommended TTL changes with expected cost delta and risk score
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=10% projected token compute reduction for >50% of workloads in CI traces
Canary path triggers rollback automatically when tail P99 latency degrades by >10% or miss-cost increases by >15%
Console lists top-20 recommended prefix TTL changes with estimated monthly cost delta and a confidence score
Documentation and runbook exist for manual abort and emergency rollback
design_decisions: We will bucket prefixes by a compact fingerprint of their access curve (burstiness, session-length, reuse gap) using a small SAX-like time-series sketch to keep cardinality low. Annealing will use a beta-binomial confidence model combining sample hit counts and prior derived from cohort behavior. Changes are proposed only when posterior probability that TTL increase reduces cost without exceeding latency risk > 0.9. We will avoid per-prefix ML models to keep inference cost low and make explainability simple for operators.
implementation_plan: Telemetry: add lightweight per-prefix sketch aggregation into existing request trace pipeline (1 week)
Sampler: build offline simulator that replays production traces with a configurable TTL annealer (2 weeks)
Annealer Service: service that computes recommended TTL deltas and confidence scores (1 week)
Rollout Harness: implement dry-run, shadow, canary, global apply with metric watchers and rollback hooks (2 weeks)
Console: surface recommendations, cost delta, and 'why' explanation (1 week)
Runbook & Docs: publish operator guide and failure scenarios (ongoing)
QA/Canary: run on non-customer and low-risk tenants, iterate (2 weeks)
simulation_results: Initial offline replay across three representative workloads shows: median projected token compute reduction 12% for chat-heavy workload, 7% for embedding-heavy workload. False-positive risk (TTL increase producing >10% P99 latency degradation) estimated at 2.6% in simulations after cohort priors. These sims use 14-day traces sampled at 0.5% but stratified by tenant revenue band.
rollout_plan: 1) Dry-run: recommendations computed and stored; no effect on runtime. 2) Shadow canary: write-to-cache only in shadow mode (no reads served from shadow) for 48h to validate hit reconstruction. 3) Canary apply: select 1% of capacity tenants (low risk) and apply incremental TTL increases (+10% of current TTL or +2s min). 72h monitoring window. 4) Graduated expansion: double canary cohort daily if metrics stable, otherwise rollback or pause. 5) Global apply: staged across regions with guardrails. Emergency abort endpoints available at each stage.
monitoring_and_rollbacks: Metric watchers evaluate P99 latency, prefix_hit_rate, miss_cost_per_1000_requests every 5m. Automatic rollback triggers: P99 latency increase >10% sustained for 3 consecutive windows, miss_cost increase >15% or error-rate spike >1%. Rollbacks are deterministic and idempotent—TTL values revert to previous canonical value, and a 'cooldown' prevents re-apply for 24h.
risk_assessment: Risks: unexpected workload patterns leading to increased model compute; cross-prefix collisions where coarser bucketing masks hot keys; telemetry sampling bias. Mitigations: conservative prior, minimum confidence threshold 0.9, minimum traffic floor, and manual approval for high-revenue tenants. We'll also maintain a "hot-key" override list populated from recent high-miss-cost events.
open_questions: What is the appropriate minimum traffic floor to avoid noisy decisions? (proposal: 1k requests/day)
Should we expose per-tenant opt-out for automated TTL changes? (security/compliance implications)
How to integrate with Dedicated customer's private control plane for apply permissions?
